Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 96, verse 1–8:

The interpretation of His saying, majestic is He and sanctified are His names: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he did not know. No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return.﴾

His saying, may His majesty be exalted: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾ means: O Muhammad (ﷺ), recite, mentioning your Lord, ﴿who created﴾. Then He explained who created, saying: ﴿created man from a clinging substance﴾, meaning: from blood. He said "from clinging substance" (ʿalaq), and what is intended is "from a clot" (ʿalaqah), since He went to the plural, as one says "shajarah" and "shajar" (tree and trees), "qaṣabah" and "qaṣab" (reed and reeds), and likewise "ʿalaqah" and "ʿalaq". He said "from ʿalaq" while "man" (al-insan) is in singular form, because it has the meaning of a plural, even though it is singular in form; therefore it was said "min ʿalaq".

* *

His saying: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾

He says: Recite, O Muhammad, and your Lord is the Most Generous, ﴿who taught by the pen﴾, teaching His creation writing and script.

As it was narrated:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, he recited until reaching ﴿taught by the pen﴾, and said: The pen is a great blessing from Allah; were it not for it, [affairs] would not be established, and life would not be set right. It was also said: this is the first surah revealed in the Qur'an to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

* Ahmad ibn ʿUthman al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Nuʿman ibn Rashid say, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, that she said: The first thing with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was begun in revelation was true dreams; he would see a dream and it would come like the break of dawn. Then solitude became dear to him, so he would seclude himself in the cave of Hira, worshipping therein for many nights before returning to his family; then he would return to his family and take provisions for the like, until the Truth came upon him suddenly and came to him, and said: "O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah said: "So I knelt on my knees while standing, then I returned with my shoulders trembling. Then I entered upon Khadijah and said: 'Cover me, cover me,' until the fear left me. Then he came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, I am Gabriel, and you are the Messenger of Allah.' He said: I had almost thrown myself from a precipice [from a mountain], but he appeared to me when I was resolved upon that, and said: 'O Muhammad, I am Gabriel, and you are the Messenger of Allah.' Then he said: 'Read.' I said: 'What shall I read?' He said: He seized me and pressed me three times, until I was overcome with exertion. Then he said: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, so I read. Then I came to Khadijah and said: 'I have feared for myself,' and I told her my account. She said: 'Rejoice, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. By Allah, you join the ties of kinship, speak the truth, convey trusts, bear the burdens of others, honour the guest, and help in the calamities of truth.' Then she set out with me to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad. She said: 'Listen to your nephew's son.' He questioned me, and I told him my account. He said: 'This is the Namus (divine law-bearer) that was sent down to Moses (ﷺ). Would that I were a young man in it! Would that I were alive when your people expel you.' I said: 'Will they expel me?' He said: 'Yes, no man has ever come with what you have come with except that he was opposed. If I live to see your day, I will help you with a mighty help.' Then the first of the Qur'an revealed to me after ﴿Read﴾ was: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed you are of a great character. So you will see and they will see﴾, and ﴿O you who wraps himself, arise and warn﴾, and ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ʿUrwah narrated to me that ʿAʾishah informed him, and he mentioned something similar, except that he did not say: "Then the first of the Qur'an revealed to me... to the end of the statement."

* Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad narrated to us, saying: Gabriel came to Muhammad and said: "O Muhammad, read." He said: "What shall I read?" He said: he embraced him, then said: "O Muhammad, read." He said: "What shall I read?" He said: ﴿in the name of your Lord who created﴾ until reaching ﴿taught man that which he did not know﴾. He said: Then he came to Khadijah and said: "O Khadijah, I do not think I have seen [this] except that it has come upon me." She said: "No, by Allah, your Lord would not do that to you, and you have never committed an indecency." He said: Khadijah came to Waraqah and informed him of the matter. He said: "If you are truthful, your husband is indeed a prophet, and he will face hardship from his people. If I live to see him, I will surely believe in him." He said: Then Gabriel delayed upon him, so Khadijah said to him: "I think your Lord has forsaken you." Then Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still. Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾.

* Ibrahim ibn Saʿid al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah—Ibrahim said: Sufyan said: "Ibn Ishaq preserved it for us"—that the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾.

* ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, that the first surah revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: The first surah revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾.

* He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say, and he mentioned something similar.

* Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi informed us, saying: We were in the congregational mosque, and our reciter was Abu Musa al-Ashʿari; it is as if I see him between two white garments. Abu Raja' said: From him I learned this surah: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, and it was the first surah revealed upon Muhammad.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from some of his companions, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Yasar, who said: The first surah revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The first thing revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾. Ibn Mahdi added: and ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say: The first thing revealed of the Qur'an was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾.

* He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi, who said: Indeed I see Abu Musa reciting the Qur'an in the mosque of Basra, wearing two white garments; from him I learned ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, and it is the first surah revealed upon Muhammad (ﷺ).

* He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The first surah revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, then ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿taught man that which he did not know﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: He taught man writing by the pen, which he did not know, along with other things which He taught him and which he did not know.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

He says: Indeed, to your Lord, O Muhammad, is their return, so he who tastes from His painful punishment that which he has no power to bear.

He said: Then he came to Khadijah and said: "O Khadijah, I do not think I have seen [this] except that it has come upon me." He said: "If you are truthful, your husband is indeed a prophet, and he will face hardship from his people. If I live to see him, I will surely believe in him." * He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi, who said: Indeed I see Abu Musa reciting the Qur'an in the mosque of Basra, wearing two white garments; from him I learned ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, and it is the first surah revealed upon Muhammad (ﷺ).

* He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The first surah revealed was ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, then ﴿Nun. By the pen﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿taught man that which he did not know﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: He taught man writing by the pen, which he did not know, along with other things which He taught him and which he did not know.

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿taught man that which he did not know﴾: He taught man the writing of letters by the pen.

* *

His saying: ﴿No!﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: It is not thus that man should be, that his Lord bestows favour upon him by perfecting his creation and teaching him what he did not know, and bestowing upon him what has no equal, and then he disbelieves in his Lord who did this to him, and transgresses against Him, when he sees himself self-sufficient.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾

He says: Indeed man exceeds his limit and exalts himself against his Lord, so he disbelieves in Him, because he sees himself as self-sufficient. It was said: "when he sees himself self-sufficient" [uses] "ra'a" needing a subject and predicate, and so the Arabs do with every verb that requires a noun and a verb, when the speaker makes the action fall back upon himself, pronominalizing it, saying: "When do you see yourself going out?" and "When do you consider yourself travelling?" When the verb requires only one object, they put the reflexive pronoun in its place, saying: "You killed yourself" (qatalta nafsaka), and they did not say "qatalatka" nor "qatalahu."

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾

He says: Indeed, to your Lord, O Muhammad, is their return, so he who tastes from His painful punishment that which he has no power to bear.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 96, verses 9–10:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids (9) a servant when he prays (10)?﴾

It is mentioned that this verse and what follows were revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, for he said, as we have been informed: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely trample his neck." It is also mentioned that he had forbidden the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from praying. So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Have you seen, O Muhammad, Abu Jahl, who forbids you to pray at the Maqam (the Station of Ibrahim), while he turns away from the truth and denies it?" Exalted is His remembrance, He marvels at His Prophet and the believers at the ignorance of Abu Jahl and his audacity toward his Lord, in forbidding Muhammad from praying to his Lord, while he, despite His favours upon him, denies Him.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays﴾, he said: It is Abu Jahl, who forbade Muhammad (ﷺ) when he prayed.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays﴾: it was revealed concerning the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, because he said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely trample on his neck." So Allah revealed what you hear.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays﴾, he said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad (ﷺ) praying, I will surely trample on his neck." Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 96, verse 11–19:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Have you considered if he were upon guidance (11) or enjoined righteousness (12)?﴾

.

Almighty God says: ﴿Have you considered if he [Muhammad] were upon guidance﴾, meaning: upon uprightness and rectitude in his prayer to his Lord, ﴿or enjoined righteousness﴾, or Muhammad commanded this one who forbids prayer, [to act] with piety towards God and fear of His punishment.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿Have you considered if he were upon guidance or enjoined righteousness?﴾: "Muhammad was upon guidance and enjoined righteousness."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Have you considered if he denied and turned away (13)?﴾

Almighty God says: ﴿Have you considered if he denied﴾ Abu Jahl the truth with which He sent Muhammad, ﴿and turned away﴾, meaning: he turned his back on it and did not confirm it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Have you considered if he denied and turned away?﴾: meaning Abu Jahl.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Does he not know that God sees (14). No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock (15), a lying, sinning forelock (16). Then let him call his associates (17). We will call the guards of Hell (18). No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near (19).﴾

Almighty God says: Does Abu Jahl not know, when he forbids Muhammad from worshipping his Lord and praying to Him, that God sees him, so that he fears His vengeance and punishment? It has been said: "Have you considered the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you considered if he were upon guidance...?", the phrase "have you considered" being repeated three times in alternation. The meaning is: Have you considered the one who forbids a servant when he prays, while he is a denier and turns away from his Lord? Does he not know that God sees him?

* *

As for His saying, ﴿No!﴾

He says: It is not as he claimed, that he would trample the neck of Muhammad; that is, he is not able to do that and cannot reach him.

* *

His saying: ﴿If he does not desist﴾

That is: if Abu Jahl does not desist from Muhammad, ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾, that is: We will take hold of the front of his head, humiliating him and disgracing him. It is said from this: "I seized his hand" when I took hold of his hand. It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾ is: We will blacken his face, and mention of the forelock suffices for the whole face, since the forelock is at the front of the face. It has also been said that the meaning is: We will take him by his forelock to the Fire, as He said: ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿a lying, sinning forelock﴾

Here "forelock" is in the genitive (khafd) as a repetition returning to the first "forelock", and the forelock is described with lying and sin, the meaning being [that these qualities belong to] its owner.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾

Almighty God says: Then let Abu Jahl call the people of his assembly and his helpers, from his clan and his people. Al-nadi (the assembly) is the gathering place.

It was said, as has reached us, that this was said because when Abu Jahl forbade the Prophet ﷺ from praying at the Maqam, the Messenger of God ﷺ rebuked him and spoke harshly to him, so Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad threaten me, when I am the one with the most associates in the valley?" Then God, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾, so let him then call his associates; for if he calls his associates, We will call the guards.

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said concerning this, and those who interpret the Qur'an have said so.

Mention of the reports transmitted on this:

✱ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Jami' narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, both from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was praying at the Maqam when Abu Jahl ibn Hisham passed by him and said: "O Muhammad, did I not forbid you from this?" and he threatened him. The Messenger of God ﷺ spoke harshly to him and rebuked him, so he said: "O Muhammad, with what do you threaten me? By God, I am the one with the most associates in this valley." So God revealed: ﴿Then let him call his associates. We will call the guards﴾. Ibn Abbas said: Had he called his associates, the guards of punishment would have seized him at that very moment.

✱ Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was praying when Abu Jahl came to him and forbade him to pray, so God revealed: ﴿Have you considered the one who forbids a servant when he prays?﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿a lying, sinning [forelock]﴾. He said: "He knows that I am the one with the most associates in this valley." The Prophet ﷺ became angry and said something; Dawud said: I did not memorize it. Then God revealed: ﴿Then let him call his associates. We will call the guards﴾. Ibn Abbas said: By God, had he done so, the angels would have seized him from his place.

✱ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from his father, saying: Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Abu Jahl said: "Will Muhammad rub his face in the dust among you?" It was said: "Yes." He said: "By al-Lat and al-Uzza, if I see him praying like that, I will surely trample his neck; I will surely rub his face in the dust." He said: So he came to the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was praying, intending to trample his neck. He said: Suddenly they saw him retreating on his heels and shielding himself with his hands. He said: It was said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Indeed between me and him is a trench of fire, and terror, and wings." He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him limb by limb." He said: And God revealed, I do not know whether in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah or not: ﴿No! Indeed man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return. Have you considered the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you considered if he were upon guidance or enjoined righteousness? Have you considered if he denied and turned away?﴾, meaning Abu Jahl, ﴿Does he not know that God sees? No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock, a lying, sinning forelock. Then let him call his associates﴾, [meaning] his people, ﴿We will call the guards﴾, the angels. ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.﴾

✱ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from al-Walid ibn al-Ay'zar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If Muhammad returns to pray at the Maqam, I will surely kill him." So God revealed: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord﴾ until reaching this verse: ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock, a lying, sinning forelock. Then let him call his associates. We will call the guards﴾. The Prophet ﷺ came while praying, and it was said to him: "What prevents you?" He said: "Between me and him has become black the battalions..." Ibn Abbas said: By God, had he moved, the angels would have seized him while the people looked on at him.

✱ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Adi narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of God ﷺ praying near the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him until I trample his neck." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly."

Those who interpreted the meaning of "al-nadi" have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

✱ Muhammad ibn Mas'ad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾, he said: "Then let him call his supporters."

✱ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We will call the guards﴾, he said: "The angels."

✱ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl: "The guards, their feet are in the earth and their heads are in the sky."

✱ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿We will call the guards﴾, the Prophet ﷺ said: "If Abu Jahl had done so, the guards, the angels, would have seized him openly."

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿We will call the guards﴾, he said: "The angels."

✱ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying "the guards": "The angels."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No!﴾

Almighty God says: The matter is not as Abu Jahl says, when he forbids Muhammad from worshipping his Lord and praying to Him, ﴿Do not obey him﴾. He, mighty is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Do not obey Abu Jahl in what he commands you of abandoning prayer to your Lord, ﴿but prostrate﴾ to your Lord, ﴿and draw near﴾ to Him, by seeking closeness to Him through obedience, for Abu Jahl will never be able to harm you, and We will protect you from him.

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near﴾: it was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, who said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely trample his neck." So God revealed: ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.﴾ The Prophet of God ﷺ, when he heard what Abu Jahl had said, said: "If he had done so, the guards would have snatched him away."

End of the commentary on the surah "Read in the name of your Lord", and praise be to God alone.

✱ Muhammad ibn Mas'ad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾, he said: "Then let him call his supporters."

✱ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We will call the guards﴾, he said: "The angels."

✱ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl: "The guards, their feet are in the earth and their heads are in the sky."

✱ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿We will call the guards﴾, the Prophet ﷺ said: "If Abu Jahl had done so, the guards, the angels, would have seized him openly."

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿We will call the guards﴾, he said: "The angels."

✱ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying "the guards": "The angels."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿No!﴾

Almighty God says: The matter is not as Abu Jahl says, when he forbids Muhammad from worshipping his Lord and praying to Him, ﴿Do not obey him﴾. He, mighty is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Do not obey Abu Jahl in what he commands you of abandoning prayer to your Lord, ﴿but prostrate﴾ to your Lord, ﴿and draw near﴾ to Him, by seeking closeness to Him through obedience, for Abu Jahl will never be able to harm you, and We will protect you from him.

✱ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near﴾: it was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, who said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will surely trample his neck." So God revealed: ﴿No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.﴾ The Prophet of God ﷺ, when he heard what Abu Jahl had said, said: "If he had done so, the guards would have snatched him away."

End of the commentary on the surah "Read in the name of your Lord", and praise be to God alone.
